messages:
Alex: Heads-up — CI microbench failed on PR #5178 (kv-cache eviction microbench). Diff +12.4% vs baseline, crosses our 5% threshold. Link: https://ci.redwood/arti/5178/diff
ci-bot: Benchmark runner finished. Test: runtime/kv_eviction_microbench — mean latency 184.2ms (baseline 163.8ms) — +12.4%. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/arti/5178/artifacts, flamegraph: https://ci.redwood/arti/5178/flame.html :warning:
Priya: Ugh. Did CI attach the commit range it tested?
ci-bot: Commits tested: base=main@1769801022..head=PR-5178@1771998000. Failing commit appears between 1769900000..1771998000 (run bisect recommended).
Marc: I can take a quick bisect locally. Re-running the microbench in docker now: `./tools/run_bench --suite kv_eviction --iters 200`
Kira: If it's kv eviction, check the recent KV cache change from LRU->TTL eviction we merged last week (PR 5163). That touched the cache compaction path and kernel selector hints.
Marc: Running first half of bisect now. Local baseline (1769950001) matches CI baseline. First suspect (1770054321) already shows +9% here. Collecting perf counters.
Sam: Is this a rollout blocker? If leaking perf we should pin the rollout.
Alex: Marked as rollout-blocker on the PR and flagged infra-alerts. Please triage ASAP. :rotating_light:
Priya: Can someone paste the top stack traces? CI artifact has a full flame but it's noisy.
Marc: Copying the hot stacks from my local perf sample:
```
runtime::kv::evict_candidates
runtime::batch_scheduler::select_kernel
kernel_selector::score_for_sequence_len
nvptx::launch_attention_kernel
```
Looks like kernel selection cost increased — more time in score_for_sequence_len and the scheduler path.
Kira: That aligns with my quick profiler — extra calls to compute kernel scores for each batch due to a change to always recompute hints after compaction. I pushed a branch that caches the last hint per worker: `fix/cache-hint-per-worker`
Marc: Patch applied locally, re-ran bench: mean latency 165.1ms (baseline 163.8ms) -> +0.8%. That's within noise. So the hint recompute looks like the culprit.
Alex: Great catch. Can we get a minimal patch to revert the always-recompute behavior, keep compaction, and add a unit test?
Kira: Yep — opened PR 5180 with the revert+test. CI queued microbench job attached.
ci-bot: PR 5180: microbench job queued. Link: https://ci.redwood/arti/5180/queue
Priya: While we wait for CI on 5180, what's the rollback plan if it still fails?
Sam: If 5180 doesn't resolve it, we should revert PR 5163 (the TTL compaction change) on main, run a canary, and then reintroduce compaction with more conservative hint logic.
Marc: FYI I also collected KV cache stats: eviction scans per-second jumped 2.6x on the bad commit, and hint recompute calls per-op went from ~0.02 to ~0.9. That's a big signal.
Alex: OK — priority ordering: 1) verify 5180 microbench passes; 2) if pass, merge and unmark rollout-blocker; 3) if fail, revert 5163 and open a follow-up. Keep me posted in-thread.
ci-bot: PR 5180 microbench complete: mean 164.2ms (baseline 163.8ms) — +0.25% — within threshold. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/arti/5180/result
Priya: Nice. Can someone add a regression test that runs the microbench in CI on PRs that touch kv/cache/*? We keep missing these diffs.
Kira: Filed issue #1387 to add a presubmit microbench hook and a lightweight perf unit that asserts hint-recompute counts.
Sam: Thx everyone. Removing rollout-blocker tag from PR 5178 now that 5180 will land as a dependent fix. :thumbsup:
Alex: Leaving notes in PRs and the release changelog. Good catch all around.
